stimuli.text: For centuries, the Silk Road served as far more than a conduit for commodities; it was a vibrant artery through which ideas, beliefs and technologies flowed between civilisations. Merchants traversing its (1)________ terrain, which included scorching deserts, treacherous mountain passes and desolate steppes, carried not merely silk and spices but also philosophies that would profoundly reshape the societies they touched. The exchange was remarkably (2)________. Buddhism journeyed eastward from India into China, while papermaking techniques gradually migrated westward, eventually transforming scholarship in the Islamic world and Europe. Such cross-pollination fostered a cosmopolitan ethos in bustling entrepo ts like Samarkand and Kashgar, where polyglot traders haggled in myriad tongues. Yet the route was not without its perils. Brigands lay in wait for (3)________ caravans, and the vicissitudes of politics could abruptly sever vital links. The collapse of a single empire often precipitated a decline in commerce across vast regions, illustrating how interdependent these far-flung economies had become. Historians caution against romanticising this era, noting that disease, too, travelled along these pathways; the Black Death is widely believed to have spread partly through such networks. Nonetheless, the Silk Road's legacy remains (4)________. It demonstrates that human progress has seldom been the achievement of isolated societies but rather the fruit of sustained interaction. In today's increasingly insular  political  climate,  this lesson acquires fresh  (5)________. Nations contemplating a retreat behind protectionist barriers would do well to remember that prosperity has historically flourished where borders were porous and minds were receptive.

explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:59:source:aabcddc95cb93: Four-wall area=2h(l+b)=336. With h=6 and l=3b, solve b; floor area=l×b.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:60:source:ed3af05eb144a: Relative speed to cyclist=(63−9) km/h. Train length=relative speed×18 s. The 30-s platform crossing distance is train plus platform length; subtract train length.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:61:source:ee5649c409b22: Use AB∥CD and AD∥BC to infer triangle angles. The given angle ratio splits ∠ADC between diagonal OD and side CD; then angle chase in triangle AOD.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:62:source:7154d6f81fa74: Volume V∝r²h. Radius multiplier is 4/3, so height multiplier must be (3/4)²=9/16. Convert the drop to percent.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:63:source:cff53156e0818: A corner cube cut removes three outside square patches of area s² and exposes three new inside faces of the same area. Net surface area remains unchanged.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:64:source:ad3e5b1bf0d1c: Since 42°+48°=90°, sin²42°+sin²48°=sin²42°+cos²42°=1. Also sec²30°=4/3 and cot²45°=1.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:65:source:9ccabcb4f2216: Use the empirical relationship Mode≈3Median−2Mean. Thus Median≈(Mode+2Mean)/3.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:66:source:9ad9c928ed53a: Revenue=20×7500. Costs: 20×200×25 printing +20×80 binding +2000 advertising +20×50 supply. Profit=revenue−costs.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:67:source:726265d062e85: Time for each segment: 55/11, 65/13, 120/20 hours. Average speed is total distance divided by total time, not arithmetic mean of speeds.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:68:source:04a3ab25353d7: Let initial volume be V. After removing 70 L, remaining water is (V−70)/4; then add 20 L. Set [(V−70)/4+20]/(V−50)=0.30.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:69:source:e539773c3ca86: The shape of the four pieces is unspecified; their exposed surface area cannot be calculated.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:70:source:d46f0cd04f8b1: In triangle RST, angles at R,S are half the quadrilateral's original angles. Hence ∠STR=180°−(R+S)/2; use P+Q=360°−(R+S) and P:Q=2:3.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:71:source:60402fd928c7c: The median from the right angle to the hypotenuse equals half the hypotenuse. Express the two legs in terms of hypotenuse h and solve using Pythagoras.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:72:source:2ea2aae37ca29: cosA=√3/2 gives A=30°. Substitute tanA=1/√3, cotA=√3, secA=2/√3 in the fraction.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:74:source:3debb923abee6: At the encounter, total distance travelled by the two travellers is 2×300. Their combined speeds are 70+50 km/h, giving encounter time 600/120=5 h; Shivam is 250 km from P.
explanations.cgl-2026-10-07:q:83:source:67227e4c930f8: The published option changes grammatical tense/aspect; none is an exact active equivalent.
